items.title: PhET Expression Exchange
items.why: You drag coin tiles worth x, y and 1 into a pile and watch the expression collect its own like terms, so combining terms stops being a rule and becomes something you can see.

items.title: Polypad Algebra Tiles
items.why: An infinite canvas of algebra tiles you can drag, duplicate and arrange, which is the fastest way to see why 3x plus 2x is 5x but 3x plus 2 is not.

items.title: NRICH Algebra for Secondary Students
items.why: Cambridge University's problem index, ad-free, where the questions are genuine puzzles with a hidden trick rather than twenty of the same exercise in a row.

items.title: SolveMe Mobiles
items.why: Hanging-mobile puzzles that are linear equations in disguise; you balance the shapes and only afterwards realise you just did the same-operation-to-both-sides move.

items.title: PhET Equality Explorer
items.why: A balance scale that tips the moment you do something to one side and not the other, which makes the reason for the rule obvious instead of memorised.

items.title: Graspable Math Canvas
items.why: You physically drag terms across the equals sign and the app refuses moves that break the equation, so you get instant feedback on every step of a solve.

items.title: PhET Equality Explorer: Two Variables
items.why: The same balance scale but with two unknowns at once, which is the clearest demonstration of why one equation is never enough to pin down two values.

items.title: Desmos Graphing Calculator
items.why: Type both equations, then click the crossing point and Desmos names its coordinates for you, so you can check an algebraic solution graphically in about ten seconds.

items.title: GeoGebra Calculator Suite
items.why: Its algebra view solves a system symbolically and shows the lines at the same time, so you can compare substitution, elimination and the graph side by side.

items.title: PhET Function Builder
items.why: You literally build a machine out of chained function blocks and feed cards through it, which is the same mental model as writing a function in a script.

items.title: Mathigon: Relations and Functions
items.why: An interactive chapter that makes you drag the mapping arrows yourself, so the one-input-one-output rule is something you test rather than read.

items.title: GeoGebra Graphing Calculator
items.why: Plot a relation and drag a vertical line across it to run the vertical line test by hand, which is faster than arguing about it on paper.

items.title: PhET Graphing Lines
items.why: Its Line Game mode scores you on turning an equation into a graph and back again under time pressure, which is exactly the skill a slope question tests.

items.title: Mathigon: Rates of Change
items.why: Builds slope up from real rate-of-change scenarios rather than from the rise-over-run formula, which is why the Nether portal ratio and slope turn out to be the same idea.

items.title: Desmos Graphing Calculator
items.why: Type y = mx + b and Desmos offers you sliders for m and b, so you can watch the line tilt and shift and connect each number to what it does.

items.title: Mathigon: Piecewise Functions
items.why: Interactive graphs where you move the boundary and watch which branch takes over, which is the whole point of a piecewise definition.

items.title: Desmos Graphing Calculator
items.why: Desmos takes restriction syntax directly, so typing y = -x {x < 0} and y = x {x >= 0} draws the two branches separately and shows exactly where they meet.

items.title: Mathigon: Sequences and Growth
items.why: Starts with geometric sequences and constant ratios, which is the cleanest way to see why a doubling farm is exponential and a level cost is not.

items.title: Mathigon: Carbon Dating
items.why: A worked interactive on exponential decay with a half-life, which is the decay case you rarely get to play with in a textbook.

items.title: GeoGebra Graphing Calculator
items.why: Put a slider on b in y = a * b^x and drag it through 1 to see growth flip to decay at the exact moment the base crosses one.

items.title: PhET Projectile Motion
items.why: Fire things at a target, turn air resistance on and off, and see for yourself how much drag bends the arc away from a clean parabola.

items.title: PhET Graphing Quadratics
items.why: Drag a, b and c and watch the vertex and axis of symmetry move, so the minus-b-over-2a formula becomes a thing you have already seen happen.

items.title: Mathigon: Graphs of Quadratics
items.why: Connects standard form and vertex form with graphs you manipulate, which makes converting between them feel like a purpose rather than busywork.

items.title: Desmos Graphing Calculator
items.why: Graph your own trajectory model, and Desmos will label the vertex and the intercepts when you click them, so you can check a hand calculation instantly.

items.title: PhET Area Model Algebra
items.why: Builds a rectangle out of algebra pieces so factoring becomes finding the side lengths of a known area, which is the same move as sizing a farm plot.

items.title: Mathigon: Solving Quadratic Equations
items.why: Derives the quadratic formula from completing the square in front of you, so the formula stops being a random string to memorise.

items.title: Didax Algebra Tiles
items.why: Completing the square with physical tiles: you actually run out of pieces and have to add the missing corner, which is where the name comes from.

items.title: Math is Fun: Distance Between 2 Points
items.why: Drag either point and the right triangle, the two squared legs and the square root all update together, which is the F3 coordinate distance calculation made visible.

items.title: GeoGebra Graphing Calculator
items.why: Plot y = sqrt(x) and try to trace left of zero: the curve simply stops, which is what a domain of zero to infinity looks like rather than what it sounds like.

items.title: Math is Fun: Squares and Square Roots in Algebra
items.why: Covers the exact trap in radical equations, that squaring both sides can invent a solution that was never there, and shows how to catch it.

items.title: Graspable Math Canvas
items.why: You drag a common factor out of the numerator and denominator and it cancels under your finger, which makes simplifying a physical action instead of a guess.

items.title: GeoGebra CAS Calculator
items.why: Factor and Simplify commands show the fully factored form of a messy rational expression, so you can find the excluded values before you cancel anything.

items.title: Math is Fun: Rational Expressions
items.why: A short, ad-light walkthrough that is unusually clear about why a cancelled factor still leaves a hole in the original expression's domain.

items.title: CODAP
items.why: Drop in your own numbers and drag attributes onto axes to build graphs in seconds, which is the tool to reach for after you have actually measured a farm rate.

items.title: PhET Plinko Probability
items.why: Run ten balls, then ten thousand, and watch the sample distribution settle onto the theoretical one, which is the direct answer to whether ten kills is enough data.

items.title: Seeing Theory: Basic Probability
items.why: Brown University's animated visual course where every idea is a simulation you can run, and it is fast and text-light on a slow laptop.

items.title: PhET Least-Squares Regression
items.why: Place your own data points, drag a line through them, and see your error scored against the true best fit, which is line-of-best-fit as a game you can lose.
